title: How to actually start with AI (3 steps)
hook: How to actually start with AI.
summary: How to start using AI properly as a beginner (3 steps that actually work)
body: How to start using AI properly as a beginner (3 steps that actually work)
My friends ask me this all the time. They flip between ChatGPT, Claude and every new tool, and never get comfortable with any of them. Here's what I tell them:

1. Stop tool hopping. Pick ONE tool (Claude or ChatGPT, I don't mind which) and use it every day for a month.
2. List the tasks you hate doing. If it's repeatable, hand it to AI.
3. Give it context. Talk to it like a colleague and show it good examples of what you want. That's where good prompts come from.
Do this for a month and you'll find AI is a lot easier than you thought.
Comment START and I'll send you my starter prompt template.
guide: This is a beginner's method for getting comfortable with AI in a month. You need a free or paid account with one assistant, either ChatGPT or Claude, and a notes app or a sheet of paper.
1. Choose one assistant, ChatGPT or Claude, and commit to using only that one every day for a month.
1. Write down the tasks you do in a normal week, then mark the ones you dislike doing.
1. Circle the disliked tasks that repeat, such as replying to similar emails, summarising notes or drafting the same document.
1. Pick one circled task and tell the assistant who you are, what the task is and who the result is for, as you would brief a new colleague.
1. Paste in two or three real examples of a good result, and say what makes each one good.
1. Ask for the task, correct what it gets wrong, then save the final wording as a reusable prompt in your notes app.
1. Add one new task each week, reusing the same context and examples, and keep your best prompts in one place.
Watch out: Don't switch tools when a result disappoints you, because the fix is usually more context and better examples, and show only good examples, since the assistant copies whatever you give it.

```
You are helping me get started with AI as a complete beginner. I will use only <ChatGPT or Claude> for the next month.
Step 1: Ask me up to 8 short questions about my job, my week and the tasks I dislike. Wait for my answers.
Step 2: From my answers, list the tasks that repeat and rank them by how much time they cost me. Recommend the three best to hand to AI first.
Step 3: For the top task, write a starter prompt template with these labelled sections: who I am, what the task is, who the output is for, tone and length, and a place for me to paste two or three good examples.
Step 4: Ask me for those examples, then show me one draft result using the template.
Step 5: Tell me how to improve the template based on what I correct.
Constraints: plain English, British spelling, no jargon, and no tools beyond <ChatGPT or Claude>. My role is <my job>. The task I most want to hand over is <my task>.
Return: the ranked task list, the finished template ready to copy, and a simple weekly plan for adding one new task at a time.
```
